title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: over a base X, M is a quasi-coherent O_X-module, graded (by a group, ultimately Z), with a coalgebra structure Δ: M → M⊗M. V(M) is the 'generic algebra' functor A ↦ V(M)(A) = Hom_O(M, A), i.e. V(M) = Spec Sym(M). Dualising Δ gives an A-bilinear multiplication (xy)(m) = Σ x(m')y(m''), so coalgebra structures on M are the same as algebra-scheme structures on V(M). The previous page notes that Δ is compatible with the grading exactly when this multiplication is compatible with the G-action (G = G_m, or the diagonalisable group dual to the grading group). A homomorphism Z → Z/2, equivalently μ_2 → G, turns the grading into a mod-2 grading, so V(M) = V(M)^even × V(M)^odd.

This page makes two definitions.
(1) Δ, or the coalgebra M, is *anticommutative* if the generic algebra is graded-commutative: xy = (-1)^{deg x · deg y} yx for x, y homogeneous mod 2. Dually, the odd–odd component of Δ is skew under the flip τ, and the other components are symmetric. Grothendieck leaves the translation in terms of Δ to the reader.
(2) Δ is *alternating* if, in addition, x^2 = 0 for every odd x. Testing on the universal point A = Sym(M), this says that the component Δ^{11}: M_0 → M_1⊗M_1 composed with M_1⊗M_1 → Sym^2 M_1 is zero. The left-margin note 'verify equivalent: M → M^1⊗M^1 → Sym^2 M^1 is zero' is exactly this check.

He then proves alternating ⇒ anticommutative by polarisation: for odd x, y, 0 = (x+y)^2 = x^2 + xy + yx + y^2 gives xy + yx = 0. He remarks that both notions are stable under finite limits (reading uncertain).

Finally he announces k-coderivations and k-antiderivations (odd, parity-exchanging) of a coalgebra. These are dual to derivations and antiderivations of the O_X-algebra V(M). The next page continues with codivisions, i.e. duals of divided-power structures and 'co-PD' notions.

Purpose: to set up a coalgebra / 'dual' formalism, including the super (mod 2) case, for the divided-power de Rham complex of the 1976 IHÉS lecture. The de Rham complex is to be treated as an alternating graded object, and divided powers are to be dualised to coalgebra-side structures.
errors: No real mathematical error. The implication alternating ⇒ anticommutative is correctly proved. The converse fails when 2 is not invertible, and Grothendieck rightly states only one direction.

Margin note: the source of the map should be the even part M_0 (or M^0), and the relevant component is Δ^{11}: M_0 → M_1⊗M_1, not 'M^1 —Δ^{00}→'. This is because x^2 has even degree when x is odd. It is probably a slip or a misreading.
The claimed stability 'par limites finies' is plausible but not argued; the transcribed reading is uncertain.

ideas.what: Coalgebra structure on M is equivalent to an algebra law on the functor V(M) = Hom(M, -). The coalgebra is studied through its 'generic algebra' as an algebra scheme.
ideas.modern_name: Linear (Cartier-type) duality between coalgebras and algebra functors/schemes; functor-of-points description of coalgebras
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA 3 (V(M), functor of points); not this exact formulation

ideas.what: Z/2-grading obtained from a homomorphism μ_2 → G (G the group acting via the grading)
ideas.modern_name: Parity from a central μ_2 (super-structure via ε: μ_2 → G)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Catégories tensorielles (2002), for the systematic super-Tannakian use; Koszul sign rule is classical

ideas.what: Anticommutative (graded-commutative) versus alternating (strictly graded-commutative, x^2 = 0 for odd x) coalgebras, defined via the dual generic algebra; alternating ⇒ anticommutative by polarisation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Bourbaki Algèbre III; Illusie, Complexe cotangent)

ideas.what: Coderivations and anti-coderivations of a coalgebra, dual to derivations/antiderivations of V(M); preparation for 'codivisions' dual to divided powers
ideas.modern_name: Coderivations of coalgebras; duality between PD structures and coalgebra structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (coderivations in Quillen, Stasheff); PD/differential-operator duality in Berthelot

deep.surprise_reason: This is foundational bookkeeping: graded-commutative versus alternating coalgebras, formulated via the dual algebra functor V(M), with a standard polarisation argument. The only mildly notable features are getting the super-grading from μ_2 → G and the coalgebra-side programme for divided powers, which belongs to the larger (unpublished) lecture project rather than this page.
transcription_corrections: Margin: the map should read M^0 (or M_0) → M^1⊗M^1 → Sym^2 M^1 via the component Δ^{11}, not 'M^1 —Δ^{00}→'. The handwriting is cramped; the content requires the even source.

'On laisse au lecteur le soin de dégraduation cette condition': the verb is uncertain. The intended sense is 'to translate (express) this condition in terms of Δ'; the transcribed word is not grammatical.
'et donc {+par+} la coalgèbre aussi l'Algèbre est anticommutative' is better read as 'et donc (pour la coalgèbre aussi) l'Algèbre est anticommutative, i.e. alternance ⇒ anticommutativité'.
'se conservent par limites finies': the reading is uncertain (possibly 'limites projectives' or 'produits').
